entries.label: Aleutian, Alaskan Stream and North Slope identities
entries.summary: Aleutian/Subarctic eastward flow, westward Alaskan Stream and Bering-side Aleutian North Slope flow are distinct. The roughly 20 km North Slope width is not an Aleutian width. Western SST-front search bounds do not define a current axis, endpoints or paired width edges. Whole-current dimensions remain unresolved.

entries.label: Modern regional mean versus historical surface assessment
entries.summary: Modern observations support mean northward flow at 26.5 N, distinct from the older northern surface-flow assessment. Neither study defines whole-current endpoint coordinates. Table 3 gives a 49.4 km coast-to-site-B transport integration span, not current width; instrument positions are not along-current endpoints. Weak August-September transport maximum does not establish seasonal route geometry.
entries.source_locator: Introduction, section 3.1, Table 1, Table 3 (PDF page 15), seasonal discussion/Fig. 11 and Conclusions

entries.label: Offshore West Australian versus coastal Leeuwin flow
entries.summary: Modern West Australian Current means broad northward offshore flow, distinct from coastal southward Leeuwin. Andrews (1977) used the name for a cyclonic stream turning poleward: its reported 800 km trough extent and 100-200 km stream width remain historical source context, not admitted dimensions for this current or seasonal extrema. Whole-current axis, endpoints, width and annual ranges remain unresolved.

entries.label: Northern-branch fitted scale versus whole North Cape system
entries.summary: 2007 observations support an approximately 8 km Northern-branch Gaussian profile scale, not paired-edge full width or a seasonal range. Whole-system route and dimensions remain unresolved.

entries.label: Atlantic subsurface reach and island bifurcation scope
entries.summary: Declared 35 Wâ€“5 E subsurface reach excludes upstream retroflections and the Sao Tome bifurcation. Surface currents, deeper jets and modeled island-generated eddies remain distinct; whole-current dimensions and seasonal geometry unresolved.

entries.label: Lower-core studied reach versus broader Mediterranean Water spreading
entries.summary: AMUSE lower-core reach around Cape St. Vincent remains separate from Gibraltar density flow, offshore water spreading and meddy loops. Regional 30 km and 10 km width metrics do not form a seasonal range; whole-current endpoints unresolved.

entries.label: Subsurface float-study reach versus whole-current extent
entries.summary: 35 Wâ€“10 W editorial studied reach in the context of 200 m floats excludes surface drift and recirculation loops. The eastern fate and whole-current dimensions are unresolved; 3â€“6 S sampling band is not width.

Section 4 [9]: mean core around 3 S at 35 W and slightly south of 4 S farther east. Sections 5â€“6: western meanders and unresolved layer-dependent connectivity.

entries.label: Separate subsurface sections and historical width scope
entries.summary: 35 Wâ€“23 W editorial reference reach connects separate observational neighborhoods, not a continuous observed axis. Historical month-dated two-degree latitude widths convert to approximately 220 km section spans; transport boxes and seasonal strength are not current dimensions.
entries.source_locator: Bourles et al. (1999), section 4.8, p. 21163: 35 W NEUC centered at 5 N in February 1993 and April 1996; core near sigma-theta 26.75. Sections 4.6 and 6.1 separate source retroflection from the named current; eastern filament context cites earlier work.

entries.label: Ligurian studied segment within Northern Current
entries.summary: The ledger treats Ligurian Current as a Northern Current segment. This studied reach overlaps the broader current geography; do not add its length to the parent or count it as an independent parallel flow. Surface sampled Genoaâ€“Menton/Nice reach retains editorial gates. Local 15â€“35 km offshore profile band supplies approximately 20 km span; no whole-current or seasonal width inferred.

entries.label: East Adriatic naming and extent convention
entries.summary: Eastern-coast northwestward circulation convention is distinct from the western return and basin gyres. Otranto-to-Istria context is not a diagnosed whole-current axis; Dalmatian-name overlap remains unresolved, and 800 km basin length is not current length.
entries.source_locator: Section 2.1 and Figure 1 caption: northwestward eastern-coast EAC, separate southeastward western-coast WAC, three sub-basin recirculations, wind modulation.

entries.label: Black Sea closed-circuit scope and state exclusions
entries.summary: Declared closed reference circuit excludes interior gyres, coastal eddy loops and seasonal continuity claims. MEDI/REDS raw display contacts are geographic mask artifacts, retained in the audit and excluded from navigation.
entries.source_locator: Introduction; Section 2; Sections 3.1 and 3.2.1: surface geostrophic context, seasonal anomalies and Rim circuit around interior gyres.

entries.label: Coastal studied reach, northern uncertainty and local threshold width
entries.summary: The 66 N to Cape Farewell editorial reach is separate from the source approximately 1000 km shelf survey. Weak northern identification and merging near 63 N limit continuity claims. The 30 km Cape Farewell width uses a 15% inner-jet velocity threshold and cannot buffer this whole route or supply annual margins.
entries.source_locator: Sutherland and Pickart (2008), section 3: Cape Farewell and 66 N section geography; section 3.5: weak assumed northern jet near 68 N; sections 8-9: merging near 63 N and approximately 1000 km shelf survey description. Relevant text inspected, no current-axis figure digitized.

entries.label: Naming convention and Atlantic branch scope
entries.summary: NOAA Norwegian Current is a broad northeastward off-Norway naming convention. The modern Norwegian Atlantic Current, with separate slope and front branches, is not automatically this ledger identity or the Norwegian Coastal Current. Name equivalence remains unresolved; whole-current dimensions remain unknown.
entries.source_locator: Norwegian Current, North Atlantic Current and Spitsbergen Atlantic Current entries.

entries.label: Naming convention and Atlantic branch scope
entries.summary: NOAA Spitsbergen Atlantic Current describes northwestward flow off southwest Spitsbergen. The modern West Spitsbergen Current is a northward Atlantic-water continuation toward Fram Strait. Regional overlap does not establish identical names, branches or endpoints; no existing West Spitsbergen route length is transferred.
entries.source_locator: Norwegian Current, North Atlantic Current and Spitsbergen Atlantic Current entries.

entries.label: Subsurface coastal reach versus modeled branching pathways
entries.summary: East New Ireland editorial coastal reach excludes downstream retroflection, Bismarck continuation and EUC length. Subsurface geography is not a NASA surface observation; the source model closes St Georges Channel at its resolution. Exact layer, dated geometry, whole-current width and annual margins remain unresolved.
entries.source_locator: Grenier et al. (2011), Introduction [5] and Figure 1 caption: NICU along eastern New Ireland and separate NGCU/SICU; section 2.1 [12]â€“[15]: 0.25-degree model and gateway limitations; section 3.2 [22] and coastal pathway discussion. entries.label: Subsurface PNG reach, mooring support and boreal source seasons
entries.summary: Northern PNG editorial reach is separate from the seasonally reversing surface New Guinea Coastal Current. The source uses boreal labels south of the equator; its local 150–250 m undercurrent core and ENSO shoaling do not provide annual path or width geometry. Vitiaz passage, other branches and downstream EUC lengths are excluded.
entries.source_locator: Ueki et al. (2003), Introduction [2]â€“[7]: separate surface and thermocline flows, northern PNG coast and gateway relations; Data [8]: 142 E moorings; Results 3.1 [17]â€“[18]: local 150â€“250 m core and El Nino shoaling. Relevant text inspected; no current axis digitized.

entries.label: Source-proposed modeled flow and unresolved coastal extent
entries.summary: The source proposes Solomon Islands Coastal Undercurrent from a 1/12-degree model east of the Solomon Sea. This does not establish observed coastal continuity, complete endpoints or a dated footprint. Author abstract read; publisher full text blocked. NICU and EUC dimensions are not transferred.
entries.source_locator: Author-hosted abstract: previously unknown current east of Solomon Sea formed where SEC meets Solomon Islands; named Solomon Islands Coastal Undercurrent.

entries.label: Mean section connection versus seasonal surface expression
entries.summary: 140 W to 95 W is an editorial studied reach, not a whole-current axis. Near 110 W the source surface expression is absent in December-February and peaks in August; this does not establish absence at all depths. Source ensemble dates do not date this route; width and annual ranges remain unresolved.
entries.source_locator: Section 3.1: 140 W near-surface core around 7 N, 125 W around 8 N, southward shift at 110 W and northward rebuilding at 95 W; section 3.2.3 separates seasonal surface expression near 110 W.

entries.label: Northern Tsuchiya mean cores and integration limits
entries.summary: 155 W to 110 W is an editorial northern Tsuchiya studied reach. Local mean cores shoal from 220 m to 130 m; no uniform axis depth inferred. Transport integration latitude limits are not width. Historical compilation dates do not date the route, and the 130 E NEUC identity is kept separate. A separate Rowe et al. general 2-degree meridional width summary is now retained as approximately 220 km; the two jet records share one source claim, not independent observations or annual extrema.
entries.source_locator: Sections 2-3 and Table 1: north SSCC peaks at 155 W 3.5 N/220 m and 110 W 4.5 N/130 m. Transport integration latitude limits and 700-dbar reference are separately defined; they are not route width or a uniform axis layer.

entries.label: NEUC mooring jets versus northern Tsuchiya support
entries.summary: The 130 E NEUC mooring study concerns multiple subsurface jets farther north than the equatorial northern Tsuchiya cores. No alias equivalence or connecting trajectory is established; the Tsuchiya route length is not transferred. Transport integration bounds do not establish width.
entries.source_locator: Mean structure Results: 130 E multiple eastward jets at 8.5 N/12.5 N/17.5 N; positive velocities integrated from 26.8 sigma-theta to 900 m across 8.5-17.5 N.

entries.label: Historical southern mean cores versus primary/secondary jets
entries.summary: The 155 W to 110 W historical southern mean-core reach is one editorial connection, not a combined primary/secondary axis. Rowe et al. distinguish primary SSCC and secondary SSCC but leave independent origin versus splitting unresolved. Local 250 m/160 m mean cores do not define a uniform layer; transport integration bands and a roughly 40 km PV front are not current width or seasonal ranges. A separate Rowe et al. general 2-degree meridional width summary is now retained as approximately 220 km; the two jet records share one source claim, not independent observations or annual extrema.
entries.source_locator: Sections 2-3 and Table 1: south SSCC peaks at 155 W 3.5 S/250 m and 110 W 5.5 S/160 m. Latitude integration bands are not widths. Rowe et al. (2000), introduction and section 3e/Fig. 10 caption, distinguish primary and secondary southern jets.

entries.label: Guiana/Guyana extent and continuity conventions
entries.summary: Guiana/Guyana limits vary by source. Local French Guiana shelf observations do not establish continuous flow in every layer; North Brazil continuation and detached ring motion remain separate. No universal endpoint, current width or annual axis established.
entries.source_locator: Mooring description, sections 3.1-3.2, discussion paragraph 46 and conclusion paragraph 52

entries.label: Western summer reach versus mean section bands
entries.summary: Western summer studied reach retains branch-merging limits and editorial latitude gates. Source mean-field widths at two sections are not the selected route width, seasonal range or mean of instantaneous widths. Whole-current and annual dimensions unresolved.
entries.source_locator: Sections 2.1, 3, 4.2 and 6 / Fig. 8 caption

entries.label: Local seasonal direction and El Niño exception
entries.summary: Local upper-ocean direction composite reverses southeastward November–April to northwestward May–October. Three-cycle sampling, gaps and El Niño exceptions limit annual interpretation. Direction symbols are not current axes or measured seasonal lengths/widths.
entries.source_locator: Data and Method, sections 3.2–3.3 / Figures 4 and 9 captions

entries.label: Eastern naming convention and idealized transport reach
entries.summary: 70–90 E is a declared regional reach under the eastern SIOC naming convention. Longitude gates are approximate context, and every latitude/connecting bend is editorial. Historical upper-1000 m transport is not a fixed-depth axis; western ARC, recirculation and northeastern continuation are not summed. Whole-current and annual dimensions remain unresolved.
entries.source_locator: Stramma and Lutjeharms (1997) section 3.2; Grand et al. (2015) section 3.1.1; earlier/later naming conventions retained.

entries.label: Frontal proxies, separate-year sections and layered flow
entries.summary: The 103–88 W studied reach connects reported STF crossings sampled in 1994 and 1993. Frontal proxies are not velocity cores or simultaneous geometry. The 150 m temperature criterion does not define an axis depth; branch correspondence and whole-current dimensions remain unresolved. Layered gyre flow cannot be identified universally by the STF.
entries.source_locator: Chaigneau and Pizarro (2005), Data [5], Table 1 and STF [14]–[17]; Ridgway and Dunn (2007), section 3.4 [15].

entries.label: Historical composite and variable eastward pathways
entries.summary: Historical composite paths combine different years and observation methods. A 2019 reassessment finds multiple pathways and questions a persistent narrow front across the central Tasman Sea. The 32–36 S meander band is not current width. A single dated axis, whole-current length and annual ranges remain unresolved.
entries.source_locator: Publisher-indexed abstract and Introduction; author repository abstract. Historical comparison: Tilburg et al. (2001), Introduction, journal p. 2918, Figure 2 caption p. 2919.

entries.label: Seasonal reversal, shallow layers and counterflows
entries.summary: South of Sri Lanka, the source defines eastward June–September SMC and westward November–February NMC phases. The 77–83 E reference drawings use editorial gates and bends. Shallow surface flow, near-coastal opposite flow, equatorial jets and undercurrents remain separate. Latitude spans are not current widths; transition geometry and annual dimensions remain unresolved.
entries.source_locator: Section 5.1.5, printed pp. 63–65 / PDF indices 62–64; Figure 48 caption distinguishes August 1993 and January 1991 sections.

entries.label: Dated subsurface band and transient undercurrent definition
entries.summary: The 1–3 March 2017 section at 90 E describes a roughly 300 km meridional current/salinity band span in the 80–150 m depth range. This is a local descriptive metric, not full width at every depth or along the current. Historical longitudinal samples do not establish one simultaneous axis; overlying flow, transient structure and seasonal exceptions need separate review.
entries.source_locator: Data and Methods p. 3; Results p. 4 and Conclusions p. 5. Historical interpretation: Schott/McCreary (2001), sections 3.2–3.2.2, printed pp. 28–31.

entries.label: March-May modeled reach and threshold-core spatial width
entries.summary: March-May BRAN climatology supports a subsurface reach with OSW connecting vertices. Reported threshold-core widths vary across longitudes, not across seasons; density-layer context is separate from the three-dimensional core extent. Whole-current and annual dimensions remain unresolved. Source latitude and mooring-end-month inconsistencies are retained in the audit.
entries.source_locator: Sections 2-4 and Figure 2-3 captions

entries.label: Winter surface reach versus spectral section regions
entries.summary: December-March surface drifter context supports the editorial 50-90 E studied reach. A 6-2.5 S frequency/phase classification band at 80.5 E is not paired-edge width. Surface flow stays distinct from the deeper SEUC; whole-current and annual dimensions remain unresolved.
entries.source_locator: Sections 2.1-2.2: drifter support, 1993-2018 selection, fitted seasonal fields and December-March winter. Section 3 seasonal discussion after Figures 5-6: eastward SECC reaches about 90 E before recirculating into SEC; Figure 13 caption.

entries.label: Poleward surface/undercurrent manifestations and seasonal mean width
entries.summary: At reference 18 N, the study names poleward surface and subsurface manifestations Mauritania Current. Its 30–40 km upwelling-season mean undercurrent width is local; the equatorward shelf jet, transport window and broader surface corridor are separate. entries.label: March 1994 current band and vertically separated cores
entries.summary: March 1994 flow at 30 W spans a described 6-8 S band, about 220 km meridionally. Two eastward cores are separated by westward flow; this is not fixed-depth full width. Nearby non-detection west of 30 W does not establish basin-wide reversal. Whole-current and annual dimensions remain unresolved.

entries.label: Reported section distances and salinity-core widths
entries.summary: GOGP99 section-distance and salinity-core evidence stays separate from a whole-current axis, velocity width and annual variation. The audit preserves local numeric support and source discrepancies.

entries.label: Winter plume reach and channel branch taxonomy
entries.summary: A source-reported winter Northern Channel plume reach is about 130 km with speed above 0.2 m/s. Channel dimensions use different conventions and remain separate from current length/width. Descending branches and downstream equilibrated water need distinct identities; no whole-current or annual dimensions inferred.
